extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and attorneys seeking accelerated examination at the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes USPTO programs and proposals that accelerate patent examination, listing program-specific eligibility requirements, required filings/support documents, fees, timelines, and procedural conditions for placing applications on an accelerated track.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated Examination Program — eligibility and filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To receive accelerated treatment under the Accelerated Examination Program, applicants must file a petition to make special under 37 CFR 1.102 entitled 'Advancement of examination' and meet certain conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key requirements include: (1) the application must be filed via EFS-Web with a petition to make special along with (a) required petition fee or (b) a statement that the claimed invention is directed to environmental quality, development or conservation of energy resources, or counter terrorism; (2) the application must be complete and in condition for examination; (3) the application must contain three or fewer independent and twenty or fewer total claims, and must not contain any multiple dependent claims; (4) the claims must be directed to a single invention; (5) the petition must include a statement agreeing to have an interview; (6) applicant must provide a statement that a pre-examination search was conducted that meets certain requirements; and (7) applicant must provide an accelerated examination support document that satisfies certain requirements. See MPEP § 708.02(a). URL: http://www.uspto.gov/patents/process/file/accelerated/index.jsp

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated Examination Program — fees, goals, and terms of acceleration
rubrics_metrics.description: Program fee structure, timing goals, and how applications are placed on the accelerated track.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition fee: US $130 to request accelerated examination (no petition fee required for inventions that will enhance the quality of the environment, relate to the development or conservation of energy resources, or contribute to counterterrorism). Goal: complete examination within 12 months from the filing date of the application. Applications are placed on an accelerated examination track throughout the entire prosecution in the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Green Technology Pilot Program — eligibility and filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A pilot permitting accelerated examination for applications pertaining to clean technologies (environmental quality, energy conservation, renewable energy, greenhouse gas emission reductions) via a petition to make special under 37 CFR 1.102.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key requirements include: (1) the application must be filed before Dec. 8, 2009; (2) the application must contain three or fewer independent claims and twenty or fewer total claims, and must not contain any multiple dependent claims; (3) the claims must be directed to a single invention that materially enhances the quality of the environment; (4) the petition must include a statement explaining how the materiality standard is met if it is not clear on its face from the application disclosure; (5) the petition must be filed via EFS-Web; and (6) the petition must be accompanied by a request for early publication and the publication fee. An initial classification requirement was removed on May 21, 2010 to allow more inventions to qualify. Support document: Not Required. URL: http://www.uspto.gov/patents/init_events/green_tech.jsp

rubrics_metrics.name: Green Technology Pilot Program — terms of acceleration
rubrics_metrics.description: When and how Green Tech petitioned applications are moved onto accelerated tracks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications will be placed on an accelerated examination track in the following situations: (1) prior to the first communication on merits (first Office action); (2) any appeal to the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences; and (3) the patent publication process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Exchange / Patent Application Backlog Reduction Stimulus Plan — eligibility and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Program designed (originally for small entities) to give accelerated status to an application if the applicant expressly abandons another co-pending unexamined application, subject to conditions and timeline requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key requirements include: (1) the non-provisional application for which accelerated status is sought must be filed before Oct. 1, 2009; (2) the applicant has another co-pending non-provisional application that has an actual filing date earlier than Oct. 1, 2009, and is complete; (3) the application for which accelerated status is sought and the other co-pending application either are owned by the same party as of Oct. 1, 2009, or name at least one inventor in common; and (4) the applicant files a letter of express abandonment in the co-pending application before it has been taken up for examination. The small-entity status requirement was removed on June 24, 2010. Examination support document: Not Required. URL: http://www.uspto.gov/patents/init_events/PatentStimulusPlan.jsp

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Exchange / Stimulus Plan — terms of acceleration and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Program timing goals and fee expectations for Project Exchange / Backlog Reduction participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot program start Nov. 27, 2009; termination Dec. 31, 2010 or when 10,000 applications granted accelerated status. No fees. Applications will be placed on an accelerated examination track (1) prior to the first communication on merits (first Office action); (2) any appeal to the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences; and (3) the patent publication process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceleration based on Applicant's Age or Health — petition and evidence requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications may be accorded accelerated examination status if the applicant's age or health justifies expedited handling; requires petition to make special under 37 CFR 1.102.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key evidentiary requirements: submit a petition with accompanying evidence showing that (1) the state of health of the applicant is such that he or she might not be available to assist in prosecution if the application ran its normal course (e.g., doctor's certificate or other medical certificate), or (2) that the applicant is 65 years of age or older. See 37 CFR 1.102(c). Examination support document: Not Required. No fees. Applications are placed on an accelerated examination track throughout the entire prosecution in the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-Track Proposal — overall framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal allowing applicants to choose among three examination timing tracks to control timing and increase examination efficiency by reducing duplication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tracks: Track I (accelerated examination), Track II (standard/traditional timing), Track III (applicant-controlled delay up to 30 months prior to docketing for examination). Proposal references: 75 FR 31763 (June 4, 2010) and USPTO press release. URL: http://www.uspto.gov/news/pr/2010/10_24.jsp

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-Track Proposal — Track I (accelerated) requirements and timing goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Track I places applications in an accelerated queue for examination upon request and payment of an additional fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who submit a request and pay an additional fee will have their application placed in an accelerated queue. Expectation: first Office action on the merits within 4 months and final disposition (allowance or final rejection) within 12 months of accelerated status being granted. Applications in Track I would require a cost recovery fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-Track Proposal — Track II (standard) description
rubrics_metrics.description: Track II preserves standard examination timing and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This option involves standard fees and proceeds under current examination procedures (i.e., traditional USPTO timing and processing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-Track Proposal — Track III (applicant-controlled delay) rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Track III allows applicants to delay examination for up to 30 months prior to docketing; includes additional rules for U.S. applications based on prior foreign filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-continuing U.S. applications may have examination delayed for up to 30 months. For U.S. applications based on a prior foreign application, no action would be taken until the applicant submits: a copy of the search report from the foreign office (if any), a copy of the first action on the merits from the foreign office, and an appropriate reply to the foreign office action. After these items are received, the applicant could request prioritized examination or obtain standard processing under Track II.
